paper.title: Fairness and Privacy Guarantees in Federated Contextual Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Federated fair linear contextual bandit (fairness of exposure)
unmapped: m agents each observe their own context vectors and share a common unknown theta*
objective is fairness regret: sum over rounds of L1 distance between learner policy and merit-proportional optimal policy pi*(a) = f(theta*.x(a))/sum f(theta*.x(a')), averaged over agents
merit function f known to the agents, with minimum merit gamma>0 and Lipschitz constant L
settings.definition_quote: We abstract the problem as a federated contextual bandit setting where each of M=[m] agents are learning about actions a in D. ... observes a context vector X_t^i ... (||x_t^i(a)||_2 <= 1) ... reward y_t^i(a_t^i) = theta^* . x_t^i(a_t^i) + eta_t(a_t^i) ... eta i.i.d. sub-Gaussian with mean 0.

settings.name_in_paper: Federated fair linear contextual bandit with federated differential privacy
unmapped: (epsilon, delta, m)-federated differential privacy under continual multi-agent observation
fairness regret objective with merit function f (min merit gamma, Lipschitz L)
settings.definition_quote: a randomized multi-agent contextual bandit algorithm A = (A^i) is (epsilon,delta,m)-federated differentially private under continual multi-agent observation if ...

symbols.L_f: Lipschitz constant of the merit function f
symbols.beta_T: confidence radius squared (beta_t = max_i beta_t^i), evaluated at T

conditions: merit function has minimum merit gamma and is L-Lipschitz
theta* lies in the confidence regions with high probability (choice of beta_t)
tuning: communication with doubling gaps until ceil(T/(m d^2 log^2(1+T/d))), then every ceil(T/(m d^2 log^2(1+T/d))) rounds

source.label: theorem: fairness regret
source.quote: With high probability, \algoname\ achieves a fairness regret of \(O\left(\frac{4\nu L\sqrt{\beta_{t}}}{\gamma}\sqrt{mTd\log{(1+\frac{T}{d})} + m^{2}d^{3}\log^{3}{(1+\frac{T}{d})}}\right)\) when \(\mid\mid x_t^i(a)\mid\mid_2 \leq 1 \:\forall a,t,i\).

results.notes: Quantity is fairness regret (L1 distance between policies, averaged over agents per Definition 1) — mapped to 'other'. Theorem states beta_t but the proof uses beta_T. Paper remarks (not formally) that with beta_t = O(d log((1+mt)/alpha)) from Abbasi-Yadkori et al. this gives O~(d sqrt(mT log^2(1+mT/d))). Restated as Theorem 3 in the appendix.

symbols.L_f: Lipschitz constant of the merit function f
symbols.beta_T: squared confidence radius from Lemma 4 at time T
symbols.rho_bar: upper accuracy bound on privatizer noise-regularised Gram matrix (Dubey & Pentland)
symbols.rho_low: lower accuracy bound on privatizer noise-regularised Gram matrix

conditions: merit function has minimum merit gamma and is L-Lipschitz
tuning: sqrt(beta_t^i) = sigma sqrt(2 log(2/alpha) + d log(rho_bar/rho_low + t/(d rho_low))) + m c sqrt(rho_bar) + m z

source.label: theorem: private fairness regret
source.quote: With high probability, when \(\mid\mid x_t^i(a)\mid\mid_2 \leq 1 \:\forall a,t,i\) and Lemma~\ref{lemma:beta_potential} holds, \ourprivalgo\ achieves a fairness regret of \(O\left(\frac{4\nu L\sqrt{\beta_{T}}}{\gamma}\sqrt{mTd\log{(\frac{\bar{\rho}}{\underline{\rho}} + \frac{T}{d\underline{\rho}})} + m^{2}d^{3}\log^{3}{(\frac{\bar{\rho}}{\underline{\rho}} + \frac{T}{d\underline{\rho}})}}\right)\).

results.notes: Fairness regret mapped to 'other'. Privacy guarantee (Claim 1) is not a performance bound and is not recorded. Restated as Theorem 4 in appendix.
